finalOutput:
The game is in `snake_anthropic-claude-haiku-5-5_01.html`, and I didn't need the edit I attempted earlier. That edit was based on a wrong reading of the controls.

In CPU vs Human, `MODES.cvh` sets `cpu: [false, true]` and `labels: ['Human', 'CPU']`, so `snakes[0]` is the human. Arrow keys control `snakes[0]` through `handleDirectionKey`, so the human can steer. In Human vs Human, arrows drive P1 and WASD drives P2. The failed edit was a no-op, and the file is unchanged.

What the file contains:
- **Grid:** 30x30 canvas (600px, 20px cells) with continuous movement in four directions.
- **Growth and collisions:** the snake grows when it eats food. Hitting a wall, itself, or another snake ends that snake's run.
- **Modes:** start menu with Human vs Human, CPU vs Human, and CPU vs CPU, selectable by key (1/2/3, or Up/Down and Enter) or by click.
- **CPU AI:** BFS toward food, avoids reversing, and prefers moves that leave enough reachable space for the snake's length.
- **HUD:** mode name and live scores shown during play.
- **Pause:** P toggles pause.
- **Game over:** overlay with final scores and a winner line. Enter or R restarts with the same mode, and M returns to the menu.

Design choice to review: in two-snake modes, when one snake dies the other keeps playing until it also dies, and the higher score wins. The brief says the game ends on a wall or self collision, so if you want the whole match to end when either snake dies, that's a small change in `update()`.

I checked the file by reading it, not by running it in a browser, so I haven't tested the gameplay.

- Classic Snake on a 30x30 grid drawn on a <canvas> (e.g. 600x600 px, cell size 20 px). Dark background, clearly visible grid/snake/food colors.
- Snake moves continuously every tick (e.g. ~100 ms, can speed up slightly as score grows) in one of four directions (up/down/left/right). It cannot reverse directly into itself.
- Eating food grows the snake by one segment and spawns new food at a random empty cell (never on the snake).
- Hitting a wall or the snake's own body ends the game.
- Two snakes exist in the game: Snake 1 (Player 1 / CPU depending on mode) and Snake 2 (Player 2 / CPU depending on mode). Each has its own score displayed during gameplay. Both snakes share the same board and food. When a snake dies, the other snake keeps going; the game ends when all snakes are dead, OR for simplicity: game ends when any snake dies is NOT wanted — instead: the game ends when both snakes are dead, and the winner is the one with the higher score (or a draw). Single-player modes: only the human-controlled snake(s) matter; in cpu vs human, the CPU snake is shown in a different color. Keep it simple and robust: if only one snake is active (e.g. nothing else), the game ends when that snake dies.
- Game modes selectable from start menu: (1) Human vs Human: Player 1 uses Arrow keys, Player 2 uses W/A/S/D. (2) CPU vs Human: human uses Arrow keys, CPU snake is automatic. (3) CPU vs CPU: both snakes automatic.
- CPU snake logic: BFS (or A*) pathfinding from the snake head to the food over free cells (treat snake bodies as obstacles, the wall as boundary); pick the first step of the shortest path; avoid immediate reversal; if no path to food exists, pick any safe move that maximizes the reachable free area (flood fill) or at least avoids immediate death. Make sure CPU snakes don't just die immediately.
- Keyboard controls: Arrow keys for Player 1 (or the human), W/A/S/D for Player 2 in Human vs Human. Prevent page scrolling with arrow keys/space. Pressing P toggles pause during the game.
- Score displayed during gameplay in an HTML overlay/HUD above or beside the canvas (e.g. "P1: 0   P2: 0" or "Human: 0   CPU: 0" depending on mode), plus the mode name.
- Start menu: title "SNAKE", buttons or key choices for the three modes (keys 1, 2, 3 and/or clicking buttons), and short control instructions. Start with ENTER or click.
- Game over screen: shows the final scores, winner text (or draw), and says "Press ENTER or R to restart" / "Press M for menu" (restart with a keypress must work: Enter or R restarts the same mode immediately; M goes back to the menu).
- Restart via keypress from the game over screen (and also R during gameplay can restart).
- Use a requestAnimationFrame or setInterval loop with a fixed-tick update; make sure only one loop runs when restarting (clear old intervals).
- Clean, well-structured code with camelCase names, comments where useful, CSS in a <style> block in the head, JS in a <script> block at the end of body. Use semicolons, const/let.
- Final deliverable: a single HTML file that works when opened directly in a browser."}
